title: Bonferroni correction as a named FWER bound
dek: α/m on each test. Wikipedia union-bound recipe. Conservative when tests are dependent or when FDR was the real loss.
story: Bonferroni on Wikipedia is the union bound: P(any false rejection) ≤ ∑ α_i, so α_i = α/m buys FWER ≤ α in the worst case, even under dependence.
That worst-case gift is why it is conservative when tests are strongly positively dependent (LD blocks, the same 40 isolates driving every gene).
stats-multiple-testing already situates it. This card is the named recipe students paste into methods.
deep: Šidák assumes independence and is slightly less conservative for large m.
Holm is a stepwise FWER method that dominates Bonferroni.
Using Bonferroni when you meant FDR is a category error, not extra virtue.
m must be the number of tests you actually ran, including the ones you did not report.

visual.caption: Teaching bars: Bonferroni threshold versus BH's data-dependent threshold on a schematic mountain of tests. Not a particular dataset.

steps.title: If the scientific loss is false discovery fraction, BH was the right purchase

example.takeaway: Bonferroni buys FWER with a union bound. It is not the only honest shop.

choices: A union bound, p_i ≤ α/m to control FWER
